document.title: Colonel Tsagolov Letter to USSR Minister of Defense Dmitry Yazov on the Situation in Afghanistan
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan Déjà vu? Lessons from the Soviet Experience
document.note: Criticism of the Soviet policy of national reconciliation in Afghanistan and analysis of the general failures of the Soviet military mission. It is the first open criticism of the Afghan war from within the military establishment. Tsagolov tried to make his criticism public in an interview with Ogonek and was expelled from the Army in 1988.

key_claims: Soviet efforts over eight years failed to stabilize Afghanistan and the problem cannot be solved by military means alone.
National reconciliation failed: the population opposes the PDPA and the countryside (kishlak zone) is controlled by the counter-revolution.
The counter-revolution knows of the Soviet withdrawal decision and will not accept partial power.
A coalition government with Zahir Shah or Peshawar 'seven' figures is judged no solution; the main forces are the base of Gulbedinn and Rabbani.
The PDPA is an artificial Khalq-Parcham union, hollow and moving toward political death; Najib cannot save it.
Afghan army morale is eroding, with growing desertions expected to become massive after reconciliation ends.
